verdicts.tldr: a stray <gno-columns-sep> or </gno-columns> with no grid open ends the frame, pushing the rest of the frame's content out and orphaning its close
verdicts.details: frameKeepsColumnsTag returns false for Sep when no grid is open (`return gridOpen && frameGrid(pc)`) and for Close on `!gridOpen`, so Open calls endFrame. A typo'd separator then pushes everything after it out of the frame, and the author's </gno-frame> renders as an invalid comment, though no grid exists that could be left half inside. The doc comment ('Any other columns tag would leave a grid half inside') does not describe this case. The phrase quoted from thread 4217015266 is gfanton's, not the author's; the author's reply 4217311375 closed the whole-grid request, and the thread never raised the no-grid case. Fix: keep a Sep or Close tag inside the frame when `!gridOpen`, render it as the inert columns comment within the frame, and regenerate the two goldens.

verdicts.tldr: utils.go and utils_test.go are not byte-identical across #6297/#6298/#6299, so a landing order that drops 6299's copy either breaks the build or silently deletes FuzzScanGnoTag
verdicts.details: The PR body says `markdown/utils.go` is 'shared byte for byte with #6297 and #6298', and the ADR says scanGnoTag and its test are copied byte for byte from the gno-button branch. 6299's utils.go adds trimTagLine, which ext_frame.go:199,270 and ext_foreign.go:190,244 use. 6298's utils_test.go carries a FuzzScanGnoTag that 6297's and 6299's lack. Whoever resolves the second merge by taking one copy will either fail to compile (CI catches that) or silently lose the fuzz test (nothing catches that). The same files sit on #6297 and #6298. Fix: move trimTagLine out of utils.go, or say in the body and the ADR that it is the one addition, and bring FuzzScanGnoTag into all three branches so utils_test.go matches.

verdicts.tldr: an indented frame tag passed through BlockRich renders as a visible backslash, and the user's tag text disappears; the new golden pins that output
verdicts.details: isExtDelimiter matches the indented line, and escapeBlockHazardsImpl writes '\\' ahead of the whole line, indent included. The backslash then sits before a space and escapes nothing, and goldmark drops the tag that follows as inline raw HTML. sanitize.gno:391 documents an escaped line-leading <gno-...> as becoming 'literal text', and the unindented uppercase golden does render that way (`<GNO-FRAME>`). The behaviour predates the PR, but this PR adds a golden that asserts it, which brings it in scope. Fix: write the backslash after the leading spaces, i.e. emit the indent and then `\<gno-frame>`, and regenerate this golden so it shows `<gno-frame>`.

verdicts.tldr: when a card frame is refused (depth cap, or an attribute), its </gno-frame> closes the outer frame instead, leaving an empty bordered box and the grid unframed
verdicts.details: If the inner-frame case's Push fails at the cap, or a card tag parses as frameTagInvalid, Open emits an invalid leaf and never sets frameInnerKey. The card's </gno-frame> then falls through to `case kind == frameTagClose && open` and calls endFrame on the outer frame while its grid is still open. The transformer then ends the frame before the grid. The golden invalid_card_at_depth_cap pins exactly this: an empty section, the grid outside it, and the real outer close left as an invalid comment. The depth case needs two nested <gno-foreign> blocks; the attribute case follows the same switch by reading and has no golden. Fix: record a refused card in the parser context so the next </gno-frame> becomes its invalid leaf rather than closing the outer frame, and regenerate invalid_card_at_depth_cap.

verdicts.tldr: a raw NUL byte makes git and GitHub treat this golden as binary, so reviewers cannot see its inputs or the output it pins
verdicts.details: The file holds a literal NUL in `<gno-frame\x00>`, so git diff shows it as binary and the PR's Files tab hides the three lookalike cases and the U+FFFD output. It is the only file under gnoweb/markdown/golden that contains a NUL. The sanitize goldens already have a text-only convention for such bytes (`// INPUT_ESCAPED`, read by sanitize_integration_test.go:204), but the ext_frame harness has no equivalent. Fix: move the NUL case into ext_frame_test.go as a "\x00" string literal, or port INPUT_ESCAPED to the TestGnoExtension harness, and keep this txtar text-only.
